Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the InnoMed Devices Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are David Thompson, CEO; Rachel Kim, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Mark Reilly, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. InnoMed Devices had a productive third quarter, marked by significant advancements in our product portfolio and expansion into new markets.

Today, I will cover six key aspects of our performance:
1. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year
2. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
3. Key assumptions underlying the guidance
4. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
5. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
6. FDA approvals and CE marks obtained

Rachel will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Vasquez will follow with updates on our R&D initiatives, and then we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter and full year.

Looking ahead, our outlook for Q4 and full fiscal year 2024 reflects strong confidence in our portfolio's resilience amid a dynamic medtech environment. For the fourth quarter, we're guiding revenue to $2.62 billion to $2.68 billion, which translates to 10% to 13% reported growth and 8% to 10% organic growth year-over-year, surpassing consensus estimates around $2.64 billion. On a full-year basis, we've raised our FY2024 revenue guidance to $10.35 billion to $10.55 billion, implying 12% to 15% reported growth and 9% to 11% organic growth, improved from our previous range of $10.1 billion to $10.3 billion. This upward revision accounts for better-than-expected U.S. procedural volumes in our high-margin Cardiovascular and Robotics segments, tempered somewhat by near-term foreign exchange headwinds from a stronger U.S. dollar.

Organic growth is projected at a solid 9% to 11% for the year, propelled by a balanced contribution from volumes, pricing, and market share expansion. In Cardiovascular, our largest segment comprising about 45% of revenue, we anticipate mid-teens organic growth in Q4, powered by the ongoing ramp-up of our next-generation InnoStent Elite sirolimus-eluting stent. Since its FDA approval in June, it has secured 15% market share in U.S. percutaneous coronary intervention procedures, following adoption patterns similar to Boston Scientific's Synergy platform. Electrophysiology consumables are another highlight, with over 20% growth expected, supported by the global atrial fibrillation surge and our expanded PulseSense mapping catheter installed base, now surpassing 1,200 systems worldwide.

Our Orthopedics & Spine segment, representing roughly 25% of revenue, is set for 7% to 9% organic growth, spearheaded by the U.S. launch of the Triad Cementless Acetabular System. This system utilizes additive manufacturing to achieve 20% superior osseointegration rates in lab testing compared to competitors like Zimmer Biomet's Persona. Robotic-assisted procedures in this area surged 25% year-over-year in Q3, and with our RoboOrtho platform, we're poised to reach 150,000 annual procedures by fiscal year-end, chipping away at Stryker's Mako dominance in complex hip and knee cases.

Neuromodulation & Diagnostics, about 20% of revenue, points to high-single-digit growth, bolstered by our NeuroVibe deep brain stimulation leads for Parkinson's disease, up 18% year-over-year, and initial momentum for the AI-powered EchoAI ultrasound platform. This platform cuts scan times by 30% and is building CMS reimbursement traction. Our $450 million acquisition of NeuroLink Therapeutics in Q2 contributes around 2 points to reported growth.

Geographically, the U.S. continues as our primary growth driver at 12% to 14% organic growth, aided by pent-up elective demand and improved payer mix following COVID backlog resolution. EMEA moderates to 6% to 8% growth due to reimbursement delays in Germany for spinal implants and UK NICE reviews on neuromodulation therapies, though France and Benelux are exceeding expectations. APAC excluding China picks up to double-digit growth, with Japan PMDA nods for InnoStent Elite and robust knee volumes in Australia. China, at approximately 10% of revenue, guides to flat to low-single-digit growth amid anti-corruption measures pressuring implant pricing—challenges also faced by Medtronic and Abbott—but our Suzhou local manufacturing ramp targets 15% localization by year-end to counter FX and tariff risks.

On the margin front, our MedTech 2.0 efficiency program has generated $250 million in run-rate savings year-to-date via supply chain enhancements and G&A optimization. Q4 adjusted gross margin is expected at 68.5% to 69.5%, a 150 basis point year-over-year improvement, fueled by a shift to disposables now at 55% of revenue, 1.5% average pricing gains, and easing resin costs after inflation peaks. Raw material inflation has eased to 2% year-over-year from 8%, courtesy of our diversified Southeast Asian supplier network, lessening dependence on traditional U.S. and EU sources.

Adjusted operating margin for Q4 guides to 24.5% to 25.5%, expanding 200 basis points year-over-year, and 24% to 25% for the full year, exceeding our prior midpoint of 23.5%. This incorporates $100 million in added productivity from automation at our Galway, Ireland, and Plymouth, Minnesota facilities, where AI-driven yield analytics have lifted line efficiency by 12%. R&D spend remains steady at 12% of revenue, supporting our $2 billion pipeline, highlighted by the pivotal trial for our da Vinci-competitive OmniFlex robotic system, with first-in-human studies planned for the first half of 2025.

This guidance highlights our ability to thrive where peers like Intuitive Surgical command 60x forward multiples on robotics momentum, while broader medtech eyes 10-12% CAGR through 2028 according to Evaluate MedTech. We've factored in risks such as potential 2025 U.S. Medicare Physician Fee Schedule cuts, modeling a 2% average selling price headwind, and GLP-1 supply issues indirectly dampening bariatric orthopedics demand. Upside could come from quicker China rebound and Eurozone tenders for our imaging portfolio. Overall, we're set to deliver 11% organic growth and 25% operating margins, fueling mid-teens EPS expansion.

Now, let's talk about the impact of pricing and cost management initiatives.

These efforts were pivotal in driving our 8% core organic revenue growth and 220 basis points of adjusted gross margin expansion to 67.8% this quarter. They countered reimbursement pressures and laid the groundwork for lasting profitability. Pricing-wise, we realized a 3.2% rise in average selling prices across Cardiovascular, Orthopedics, and Neuromodulation, despite U.S. Medicare bundled payments and a 2.7% ASP clawback on pass-through devices under OPPS rules. This is our third straight quarter of positive ASP growth, up from 1.1% in Q3 2023, thanks to matured value-based pricing.

A cornerstone is our outcomes-based contracting, now spanning 45% of U.S. commercial accounts. In TAVR, akin to Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien, we reworked deals with IDNs like Kaiser Permanente and HCA, linking 15% of payments to sub-5% 30-day readmission rates. This supported a 4.5% ASP boost on Evolut PRO+ valves and spurred 12% procedure volume growth due to our superior risk profile.

In Orthopedics, battling Stryker's Mako and Zimmer Biomet's ROSA, dynamic pricing via real-world evidence from MAUDE and NSRBP data yielded a 2.8% ASP increase on Triad total knee implants. Premiums for AI navigation modules added $25 million to Q3 revenue.

By region, U.S. pricing held at +2.9% with NTAP approvals for three devices offsetting 1.2% Medicare sequestration. Europe managed 1.8% amid NICE and IQWiG reviews, aided by EU MDR pass-through for neuromodulation leads like Medtronic's Inceptiv. APAC grew ASPs 5.1% via China NRDL wins for peripheral stents, balancing Japan volume discounts. Pricing added 110 basis points to growth, with a $185 million full-year benefit.

Cost management delivered $120 million in Q3 savings, targeting $450 million annualized, expanding gross margins 220 basis points by capping COGS inflation at 2.1% despite 7% raw material hikes in titanium and polycarbonates. Our Supplier Value Improvement Program consolidated top 50 suppliers by 18%, saving 9% on electro-mechanical parts. Hedging 70% of platinum and nitinol countered 12% spot surges from EV demand. Reshoring via a $200 million Galway automation line dropped China sourcing for structural heart components to 22% from 35%, trimming lead times 28% and tariff risks.

Manufacturing gains from digital twins and Industry 4.0 included 15% yield boosts on catheter lines for Watchman FLX LAA devices, plus SAP IBP analytics optimizing inventory to 5.2x turns, unlocking $300 million in capital. SG&A cuts to 24.5% of sales stemmed from virtual rep tools slashing travel 40% post-OPTUM and AI CRM targeting high-acuity accounts, echoing Intuitive Surgical's analytics.

Strategically, this 'Margin First' approach shifts mix to high-acuity tech, with divestitures of low-margin electrosurgery lines funding bioresorbable stents at 75%+ margins. We foresee 2-3% pricing contribution to 2025 growth and 150 basis points margin lift to 69-70%, though watchful of Medicare PAMA expansions. Our 65% structural heart share readies us to outperform Abbott's Navitor.

Moving on to key assumptions underlying the guidance.

Our full-year 2024 guidance of $12.8 billion to $13.2 billion in revenue—9% to 12% reported, 10% to 13% organic at constant currency—and adjusted EPS of $8.75 to $9.00, up 11% to 15%, rests on bottom-up models, surgeon surveys, IQVIA procedure forecasts, and CRM funnel data. It anticipates share gains in Cardiovascular, Orthopaedics, and Neuromodulation amid macro and regulatory shifts.

First, procedure volumes assume 7-9% global growth, with electives at 105% pre-pandemic. U.S. (55% revenue) eyes 6-8% TAVR growth via Evolut PRO+ and 7-9% hips/knees with Mako robotics at 65% share over Stryker and Zimmer. Europe (5-7%) benefits from CardioMEMS CE renewal, up 25% in Germany/UK. China (8-10%) leverages CoreValve NRDL for 15% share vs. Abbott/Edwards. LATAM/APAC ex-China at 12-14% via Symetis valves. Risks like respiratory surges are buffered by 98% retention and $2.1 billion backlog.

Pricing assumes flat to -1% ASPs from U.S. GPO and Medicare Advantage pressures, offset by mix shifts to MitraClip G4 (+25% premium) and Triathlon cementless (+5%). China VBP may hit 3-5%, but Suzhou margins cushion; FX at 1.08 USD/EUR, 7.2 CNY/USD with 2% headwind potential.

New products add 3-4 points: $1.2 billion from ClarityX AI imaging (20% faster procedures), ReviX stimulator ($400 million), Mako placements (450 units, 75% attach). Robotics R&D ($250 million) targets 2025 endovascular launch; 85% regulatory on-time.

Regions: U.S. 8-10%, EMEA 6-8%, APAC 12-15%, ROW high-teens. Supply chain factors 5% titanium/polymer rises but 90% dual-sourcing coverage, 120 inventory days.

Value-based care adds $300 million recurring at 85% margins; demographics and obesity tailwinds offset 4-5% capex cuts. This aligns with 5.5% medtech CAGR, emphasizing clinical edges amid reforms and tenders.

Next, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

Our SG&A discipline drove major efficiencies, hitting 27.8% of revenue—down 210 basis points year-over-year and 140 sequentially—our lowest as a public company. Amid raw material inflation, FDA Class III scrutiny on NeuroFlow stents, and hospital budget strains, Q2 SG&A was $184 million, down 2% reported despite 8% organic revenue to $662 million. Adjusted, it leveraged to 27.8% from 29.9%, with $45 million TTM run-rate cuts equating to 400 basis points margin accretion, beating peers like Boston Scientific (28-30%) and Stryker (32%).

Selling expenses (65%) dropped 3% to $120 million, with revenue per rep up 12% to $2.0 million on 850 associates. Geospatial Veeva CRM optimized territories, lifting quota to 112%; 'Digital First' AR demos for NeuroFlow/Aspire cut travel 18% ($8 million saved), accelerating adoption per Mayo/Cleveland KOLs.

G&A fell 1% to $64 million via SAP S/4HANA ERP, saving $15 million on procurement/AI analytics flagging $22 million redundancies; Bangalore hub cut 15% headcount (120 roles). SBC steady at 2.7%.

U.S. (55% revenue, $364 million) improved 280 bps to 26.5% via IDN focus (HCA/Kaiser), 30% digital shift. EMEA (25%, $166 million) to 29.2% with rep pods, Brexit warehousing. APAC/EM (20%, $132 million) 450 bps better at 27.1% via hybrid model, NeuroVasc Academy certifying 2,500 surgeons.

'LeanMed 2027' targets sub-25% SG&A at $3 billion revenue, with gen AI for 35% faster pharmacovigilance and 15% rep productivity. This generated $50 million FCF, funding $250 million CardioPulse M&A in a 9% CAGR neurovascular market.

Then, R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

Our 'Innovation-First' strategy saw $265 million R&D in Q3, 10.8% of sales—up 18% year-over-year, YTD $785 million at 11.2%, toward 10.5-11.0% full-year, topping industry 8-9% medians and matching Boston Scientific. ROI shines with 22% R&D-to-new-product revenue, e.g., CardioFlow stent's $45 million.

Spend: 62% devices, 25% digital/AI, 13% manufacturing/biomaterials. Productivity up 14% on 450 Cambridge scientists and Singapore center; 15% prototyping cuts via AI.

Pipeline: 28 programs, $15-18 billion potential, 12 Q3 milestones at 85% on-time. Structural heart's NeuroValve TR enrolled 450 in U.S. IDE (95% success, 2.1% mortality vs. Edwards Sapien), FDA Q2 2025, CE review. Neuromod's AlgiaBlock SUMMIT first 200 patients (68% pain drop > Nevro), China NMPA fast-track. Digital's VitalSense CGM FDA-cleared ($12 million Q4), CE Q1 2025. Ortho's BioForge 1,000 implants (92% integration > Stryker).

Precision medicine via BioNano buyout; Siemens AI imaging cuts times 22%; 45 patents to 1,200. Spend: NA 55%, EMEA 25%, APAC 20%. FY2024 10.7%, 15+ FY2025 milestones for 12-15% EPS.

Finally, FDA approvals and CE marks obtained.

This quarter's regulatory wins—three FDA nods, two CE marks—transform our pipeline for cardiovascular, neuromodulation, and structural heart growth, backed by $250 million R&D.

FDA PMA for VascuFlow XT DES: builds on $180 million prior sales (12% share in $5.2 billion U.S. market vs. Abbott Xience/Medtronic Onyx); 98% coverage, 0.8% failure vs. Boston Synergy. 510(k)s for Delivery Catheter 3.0 (95% success) and EchoAI IVUS (92% accuracy, 18% faster). De Novo for CardioSync TAVR valve-in-valve ($1.8 billion market, 22% CAGR vs. Edwards/Medtronic 70% share; 8-10% capture).

CE MDR Class III for VascuFlow XT and NeuroGuide Pro SCS (35% opioid cut in ESCAPE trial > Nevro/Abbott; €12 million PMS). Opens EU top markets (€4,500/implant).

Diversifies from 68% NA reliance; $120 million FY25 EU incremental, PMDA/NMPA filings. 'Precision Reg' cut PMA to 16 months; four approvals vs. peers, $350-450 million 2025 revenue at 75% margins via integration. Pipeline taps $45 billion market at 6.5% CAGR.

I will now turn the call over to Rachel for a review of our financial results.

Rachel Kim:
Thank you, David. As David outlined, we delivered a solid financial performance this quarter, with revenue beating expectations and margins expanding through disciplined execution on pricing, costs, and efficiencies. Q3 revenue reached $2.55 billion, up 11% reported and 9% organic, driven by strength across all segments. Adjusted gross margin hit 68.2%, up 180 basis points, while operating margin expanded to 24.8%. EPS came in at $2.15, exceeding guidance. Expenses were well-controlled, with SG&A at 27.5% and R&D steady at 11%. For Q4 and FY2024, as detailed, we're raising the bar on revenue and margins, with key assumptions embedded for procedural recovery, modest pricing, and innovation ramps. Full-year free cash flow guides to $2.1 billion, supporting $1.5 billion in share repurchases and debt reduction. We're on track for mid-teens EPS growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Rachel. We are making significant progress in our R&D efforts. Particularly excited about our ongoing clinical trials for OmniFlex, our robotics platform rivaling da Vinci, which is demonstrating enhanced precision in preclinical models with 25% faster setup times and reduced tissue trauma. Beyond that, NeuroValve TR data reinforces leadership in structural heart, while AlgiaBlock advances neuromodulation frontiers. Our digital tools like VitalSense and EchoAI are transitioning from clearance to commercial scale, with partnerships accelerating adoption. Investments in biomaterials and AI ensure a robust pipeline addressing aging populations and minimally invasive trends. We've maintained high execution rates, positioning us for multiple launches in 2025.

Now, back to David for Q&A.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. David, on the raised guidance, how much of the upgrade is procedural volume versus share gains, especially in Cardiovascular? And any color on FX sensitivity?

David Thompson:
Great question, John. The upgrade splits roughly 60/40 between stronger procedural volumes—particularly U.S. electives now fully normalized—and share from InnoStent Elite and PulseSense ramps. Cardiovascular mid-teens Q4 organic embeds 500 basis points share. On FX, a 5-cent euro move impacts Q4 EPS by $0.03; we've hedged 60% but monitor USD strength closely.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi team, solid margins. Rachel, can you unpack the cost savings sustainability, especially supply chain amid Red Sea issues, and SG&A trajectory into 2025?

Rachel Kim:
Thanks, Lisa. Savings are structural: SVIP supplier consolidation and Galway automation are embedded, with 9% component reductions persisting. Red Sea adds 2-3% to titanium costs, but dual-sourcing covers it. SG&A heads to 26-27% next year via digital sales and AI efficiencies, targeting LeanMed sub-25% by 2027 while growing revenue.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Mark, on commercial front, how are launches like Triad and VascuFlow XT tracking in U.S. IDNs versus independents, and EMEA reimbursement outlook?

Mark Reilly:
Mike, excellent ramp: Triad hit 20% ortho share in IDNs like HCA, where robotics attach drives premiums; independents lag at 12% but catching up. VascuFlow XT at 15% PCI share, boosted by EchoAI bundle. EMEA reimbursements firm post-MDR, with Germany NUB status adding €120 million FY25; tenders in France pipeline strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
Dr. Vasquez, impressive pipeline milestones. Thoughts on AlgiaBlock competitive positioning versus Medtronic/Nevro, and R&D spend if more tuck-ins planned?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Sarah, AlgiaBlock's AI adaptive dosing yields 68% pain relief, 15-20% edge over Intellis/HF10 in modeling, with China fast-track for $2.5 billion market. R&D at 10.7% FY24 funds organic plus tuck-ins; $100 million contingency for bolt-ons like BioNano enhancing gene delivery.

David Thompson:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are well-positioned to continue our growth trajectory and deliver long-term value.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
